First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{7}$ into the above, we get

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{7})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{7})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{7})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{7}).
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{7})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{7})\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{7}) & =3\cdot [2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{7})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{7})]\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{7}) \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{7})\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{7})} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
